In [[algebraic topology]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''Čech-to-derived functor spectral sequence''' is a [[spectral sequence]] that relates [[Čech cohomology]] of a [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaf]] and [[sheaf cohomology]].{{sfn|Dimca|2004|loc=2.3.9}}

==Definition==
Let <math>\mathcal{F}</math> be a sheaf on a topological space ''X''.  Choose an open cover <math>\mathfrak{U}</math> of ''X''.  That is, <math>\mathfrak{U}</math> is a set of open subsets of ''X'' which together cover ''X''.  Let <math>\mathcal{H}^q(X, \mathcal{F})</math> denote the presheaf which takes an open set ''U'' to the ''q''th cohomology of <math>\mathcal{F}</math> on ''U'', that is, to <math>H^q(U, \mathcal{F})</math>.  For any presheaf <math>\mathcal{G}</math>, let <math>\check{H}^p(\mathfrak{U}, \mathcal{G})</math> denote the ''p''th Čech cohomology of <math>\mathcal{G}</math> with respect to the cover <math>\mathfrak{U}</math>.  Then the Čech-to-derived functor spectral sequence is:{{sfn|Godement|1973|loc=Théorème 5.4.1}}
:<math>E^{p,q}_2 = \check{H}^p(\mathfrak{U}, \mathcal{H}^q(X, \mathcal{F})) \Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X, \mathcal{F}).</math>

==Properties==
If <math>\mathfrak{U}</math> consists of only two open sets, then this spectral sequence degenerates to the [[Mayer–Vietoris sequence]].  See [[Spectral sequence#Long exact sequences]].

If for all finite intersections of a covering the cohomology vanishes, the ''E''<sub>''2''</sub>-term degenerates and the edge morphisms yield an isomorphism of Čech cohomology for this covering to sheaf cohomology. This provides a method of computing sheaf cohomology using Čech cohomology. For instance, this happens if <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is a quasi-coherent sheaf on a [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]] and each element of <math>\mathfrak{U}</math> is an open affine subscheme such that all finite intersections are again affine (e.g. if the scheme is [[separated scheme|separated]]).  This can be used to compute the cohomology of line bundles on projective space.{{sfn|Hartshorne|1977|loc=Theorem III.5.1}}
